quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color are warning signs and what do they have on them?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know that they see you.
It is not worth the effort it takes.
It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
It guarantees that they will let you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but do not see them.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield.
They are a good substitute for goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Gradually apply the brake of the good tire. Move toward the side of the road while you slow down, then stop.

questions.question: Which gives the best eye and face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: Why do riders sometimes move into another lane while turning?

options.text: They are turning too fast.
The lanes are too narrow.
They do not know how to steer.
The lanes are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Going too fast into a turn can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Without signaling so you do not distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intentions, check for traffic, and pass when safe. Signal again and return to your lane when you can.

questions.question: Why should you wear a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
It should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, when riding for protection. Many motorcycle jackets keep you cool even in hot weather and help prevent dehydration.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors make cars appear?

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride safely?

options.text: One
Three to four
Six
More than eight

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Safe motorcyclists know they are safest when they are:

options.text: Seen by other drivers.
Faster than other vehicles.
On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Safe riders know they are safest when other drivers can see them clearly. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
The pavement is wet.
You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
The sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop on wet pavement. Increase your following distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass was started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit. You can only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Slam on the brakes to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights to see ahead. Use your high beam, except when meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
Usually will not affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
Pose no risk to your operating ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Understand the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider begins to pass.
Allow several group members to pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no other motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass and return to formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is encouraged if traffic is heavy.
Is encouraged during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Is acceptable if the rider is comfortable with it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles cannot ride between two moving vehicles on a highway or one-way street. This is illegal.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because of distractions from passengers.
Happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen with riders who have less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists avoid riding in pairs when riding in a group?

options.text: A driver merging may not see both riders.
Light reflecting off both helmets may block the riders' vision.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too hard for riders on the left to exit the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should not ride side by side. Riders in pairs do not have enough room to move safely and avoid dangers.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the back of the bike.
The back of the bike jerks from side to side.
You cannot speed up.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of the bike jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk side to side. You usually will not hear the tire fail.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You should always wear reflective and bright clothing when riding a motorcycle. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
